title: Dashboard
heading: See your machine's status at a glance.
intro: Check controller connections, running services and key status information before you start building or testing.
points: Check key statuses
Bring key status information together instead of checking each module separately.
Open detailed tools
Use the overview to decide where to investigate next.
seo_description: Check bridge health, ESP32 status and performance from your pinball machine dashboard. Open detailed diagnostics directly from the overview.

title: Accelerometer
heading: Monitor table movement.
intro: With a supported motion sensor connected, check table level and see nudge, lift and orientation readings in the browser.
points: Set a level reference
Save a level reference that reflects how your sensor is mounted.
See motion readings
View pitch, roll and sensor activity when a supported accelerometer is connected.

title: Wi-Fi
heading: Manage your machine from your network.
intro: Connect your Raspberry Pi to your network and access Pinball CTL from a browser on your phone, tablet or computer. Configure your game, check its status and make changes while working on your machine, without needing a screen or keyboard connected to the Pi.
points: Access from your devices
Open the Pinball CTL interface from another device on the same network.
Check your connection
See the current network name, IP address and connection status.
Change networks when needed
On Linux with NetworkManager and the required service permissions, save a personal Wi-Fi connection in Pinball CTL. Keep console or Ethernet access available.

title: Settings
heading: Manage your project settings.
intro: Change project details, access, firmware-source and reporting preferences. Project snapshots live in the dedicated Backup / Restore module.
points: Set project preferences
Configure project identity and installation-wide preferences.
Manage installation preferences
Update sign-in credentials, the remote firmware source, log level and reporting currency from dedicated tabs.

title: Scoring
heading: Make your shots count.
intro: Set up points for targets and events, then add combinations and multipliers to create your own scoring system.
points: Award points for events
Connect events to scoring behaviour that suits your game.
Add combinations and multipliers
Use combinations and multipliers to give players reasons to try the next shot.
Build scoring and combinations
Author scoring rules, combinations and multipliers on the Pi, alongside the rest of your game's configuration.

title: Audio
heading: Set up the sounds for your game.
intro: Upload and organise sounds, create audio cues and choose where they play. Pinball CTL lets you manage sound effects, music and playback behaviour from one place.
points: Manage your audio library
Upload, name and preview audio from one workspace.
Configure cues and outputs
Configure cues and output routing so sound becomes part of the game experience.

title: Playfield
heading: Build a visual layout of your machine.
intro: Arrange the components of your machine on a visual playfield and assign keyboard controls so you can test inputs while building, even before the cabinet buttons are connected.
points: Position playfield components
Position and customise components in the visual editor.
Map inputs for testing
Assign keys such as the left and right arrows to flipper buttons, then use them in Live View to test gameplay.

title: Integrity Check
heading: Find broken or unused references.
intro: Check links between hardware, rules, layouts and assets to spot configuration issues before they cause confusion.
points: Check project dependencies
Audit dependencies across hardware, rules, layout, lighting, audio and scoring.
Review errors and unused items
Inspect reported errors and unused items to guide your cleanup.

title: ESPLink
heading: See your controller connection.
intro: Check the connection between the Raspberry Pi and ESP32-S3, view controller details and access bridge controls in one place.
points: Check connection and firmware
Check device identity, connection status and firmware information in one place.
Manage the bridge
Manage the bridge and access controller utilities without leaving the application.
seo_title: Raspberry Pi to ESP32 Pinball Connection
seo_description: Connect your Raspberry Pi pinball host to an ESP32 controller. Check bridge status, controller identity and firmware from the ESPLink interface.

title: Firmware
heading: Manage ESP firmware versions.
intro: See available firmware releases and prepare the version you want to use with your connected controller.
points: Review available versions
See available versions and release information before preparing an update.
Prepare firmware for ESPLink
Download firmware for use with the connected ESP through ESPLink.

title: Service Log
heading: Keep track of work on your machine.
intro: Record repairs, maintenance and component changes in one place, so you have a useful history to refer back to.
points: Record what was done
Log repairs, adjustments, cleaning and replaced parts, including who carried out the work.
Keep useful details
Add outcomes, follow-up notes and supporting attachments to your service records.

title: Logs
heading: Find out what happened.
intro: View and filter web, bridge, ESP and event logs to investigate how your machine responded.
points: Choose the log you need
Switch between web, bridge, ESP and event logs.
Filter messages
Filter the visible log output to focus your investigation.
